question: Which of the following expressions is representing the correct lens formula?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1/v - 1/u = 1/f**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **lens formula** is an important mathematical expression in optics that relates the focal length (**f**), the distance of the object (**u**), and the distance of the image (**v**).
 
• The correct lens formula is **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**, where:
 
 
• **v** is the image distance from the lens.
 
• **u** is the object distance from the lens.
 
• **f** is the focal length of the lens.
 
 
 
• This formula applies to both convex (converging) and concave (diverging) lenses, with proper sign conventions.
 
• **Sign convention:** Distances are measured from the optical center of the lens:
